The UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya was the longest in the history of the event and, for the first time since 2009, concluded without a final document, the T24 news portal reported. “Issues that remained unresolved in Antalya will now be discussed… Turkey made every effort to reach a compromise at the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) in Antalya, the conference’s President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change Murat Kurum said. “Regrettably, certain countries failed to demonstrate the effort and flexibility their responsibility to history demands. Turkey did everything in its power to reach a compromise in Antalya. I leave what happened here today, the deadlocked negotiations and processes to the judgment of the entire world and humanity,” he said, as cited by the TRT Haber television channel.

🇷🇺 Putin reportedly agrees to NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine The Washington Post, citing a source close to the negotiations, claims that the Russian president privately conceded that Kiev could receive security guarantees from the US and Europe analogous to Article 5 of NATO. Moscow's key condition: No NATO troops on Ukrainian territory. In exchange, Russia may see sanctions eased, though restrictions would be reinstated if Ukraine prepares a new offensive. The US also proposed withdrawing Russian forces from the border after a ceasefire, with immediate NATO deployment to Ukraine if hostilities resume. Moscow has repeatedly rejected any form of de facto NATO membership for Ukraine without formal accession. Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov previously called such schemes unacceptable. @Slavyangrad
